speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the definition of "severely impacted life expectancy" to apply for an early withdrawal under the CPF Medical Grounds Scheme; (b) whether the definition can be brought in line with the Life Insurance Association's Critical Illness Framework or the equivalent for transparency reasons; and (c) what is the reduced Retirement Sum for calculating the withdrawal amount and how is it derived.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This is because not all their listed medical conditions would result in a severely shortened life expectancy, for example, loss of hearing or loss of speech.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Conversely, there may be medical conditions which are not on their list but could still result in a severely shortened life expectancy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We, therefore, require members who wish to make withdrawals on any of these four grounds to have their medical conditions certified by doctors either from public medical institutions or on the CPF Board's panel.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is there an existing list of ailments that lead to severely limited life expectancy available for the public to consult so that they know how to apply for the scheme?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My second question is: is this application process accessible to people from all walks of life, especially the elderly who cannot understand English well, and what may be done to make this scheme more accessible to them?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The third question is regarding the $5,000 cap for the fourth criterion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How long ago was this cap of $5,000 established and whether there were considerations to increase the cap, given the higher cost of living these days?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Any member who wishes to apply for the scheme, all they need to do is to go and see a doctor on our panel.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We have a standard form for the doctor to do the certification.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: CPF Board will basically abide by the assessment of the medical expert.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So far, we have not heard of any feedback on lack of accessibility.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: When members need to use their money in the CPF prematurely, they will come to the CPF Board.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: They do not wait for us to reach out to them.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Therefore, we do not think accessibility is an issue.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The last point is about the $5,000 cap.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Therefore,  for now, I will just keep it at the $5,000 mark.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: For successful applicants for withdrawal of CPF on medical grounds, they can either withdraw the higher of up to $5,000 or the savings after setting aside.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: So, the cap is actually the higher amount that they can withdraw.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Therefore, it is not that they will be unsuccessful if they have less than $5,000 in their CPF.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On balance, it is about allowing them to withdraw more in lump sum versus keeping some of them for their monthly withdrawal.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Our assessment is that for members who are able to meet the reduced Retirement Sum, which currently is set at $40,300, just to put it into perspective, they would be able to withdraw a monthly sum of only $550 which is derived from the Department of Statistics Household Expenditure data for lower-income households.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The amount of $550 will be just sufficient to meet their basic requirements.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Another piece of information is that at $550, the amount of $40,300 can last about seven years.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, on the part of CPF, we really have to strike a balance between allowing the member to draw more as a lump sum versus having some of these savings to support their monthly expenditure.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On balance, we think $5,000 at this moment, is about the right amount.
